headline: Whole-vendor advertising spend miscoded to IT services rather than Marketing.
mechanism: Persistent account-mapping error: every invoice from advertising agency V-0006 (allowed account 7100 Marketing) is posted to 7200 IT services by clerk U-204. Not cash loss, but it misstates expense-by-nature reporting.

evidence.what: account used vs vendor allowed_accounts
memo text on every line
total misclassified

recommended_action: Reclassify the EUR 36,934.24 to 7100 Marketing and correct U-204's coding rule for this vendor.

headline: Same order billed twice at an identical amount by vendor V-0008.
mechanism: Two orders each appear twice at the identical cent amount, days apart, with no partial-delivery marker and no credit note - the signature of duplicate billing of one delivery.

evidence.what: paired identical amounts sharing one order ref
evidence.figure: 842.50 x2 (order 358022, 4 days apart); 615.20 x2 (order 358023, 7 days apart)

evidence.what: memo lacks 'osatoimitus' (partial delivery) marker
potential double-payment exposure

recommended_action: Three-way match both order pairs; recover EUR 1,457.70 if only one delivery exists per order.

headline: Same order billed twice at an identical amount by vendor V-0009.

memo text
potential double-payment exposure

recommended_action: Three-way match both pairs; recover EUR 5,145.60 if a single delivery underlies each order.

headline: Round-thousand bimonthly billing from a steel supplier - unusual but benign.
mechanism: Six exact-thousand invoices from V-0011 on its correct account (4100). Round amounts trip the round_sum test but there is no threshold breach, no duplicate and no mapping error; amounts vary (5k-9k), consistent with estimated/contract billing.

evidence.what: amounts and account
all below the 10,000 approval tier; no other test fired

headline: One freight vendor's invoices all sit just below the EUR 10,000 approval tier.
mechanism: All four of V-0012's quarterly invoices land in EUR 9,580-9,899.99, just under the EUR 10,000 department-head approval threshold - consistent with sizing invoices to avoid approval. The 9,899.99 value (one cent under 9,900) is conspicuously precise.

evidence.what: all invoices in the near-threshold band
these are the only near_threshold flags in the ledger
context: crossing 10,000 is normal here
evidence.figure: 51 invoices >=10,000 across 14 other vendors, so the threshold is not a hard block

recommended_action: Confirm whether these freight amounts are genuine and whether they should have required department-head approval.

headline: Two partial-delivery invoices per order, each under EUR 10,000 but summing over it (V-0013).
mechanism: Two order pairs, each posted 1-2 days apart as partial deliveries ('osatoimitus'), each part 4k-7k and each pair summing above EUR 10,000 - the shape of splitting a >10k order into sub-threshold invoices. The partial-delivery memo is a plausible benign explanation.

evidence.what: pair sums vs parts
memo

recommended_action: Confirm each order's full value went through the correct approval level rather than being split at invoicing.

headline: Two partial-delivery invoices per order, each under EUR 10,000 but summing over it (V-0014).
mechanism: Same split shape as V-0013: two order pairs posted 2-3 days apart as partial deliveries, each part under EUR 10,000, each pair summing above it.

evidence.what: pair sums vs parts
memo

recommended_action: Confirm the order values received department-head approval rather than being split under the tier.

headline: A single partial-delivery pair summing just over EUR 10,000 (V-0015).
mechanism: One order posted as two partial deliveries a day apart, each part under EUR 10,000, together EUR 13,330.75 - a single instance of the split shape; benign partial delivery is the likely explanation but approval should be confirmed.

evidence.what: pair sum vs parts
memo

recommended_action: Confirm the order passed the correct approval level.

headline: One German supplier is set up as three vendor records with three different bank accounts.
mechanism: VAT DE199283746 (seals maker at Beispielstrasse 14, 22525 Hamburg) exists three times - V-0003 Karrenbach, V-0004 Kaerrenbach, V-0005 KARRENBACH - each with a different IBAN. The byte-identical name_hygiene test missed it because the spellings differ by umlaut/case. Spend is fragmented across three identities, defeating duplicate and per-vendor controls, and three IBANs for one legal entity is a payment-integrity risk.

evidence.what: one VAT, three vendor_ids, three IBANs
name spellings evade byte-identical name_hygiene
combined spend, all on account 4110
evidence.figure: 23,651.32 + 15,026.40 + 10,323.64 = 48,001.36 across 15 txns; no identical cross-record amounts (distinct deliveries)

recommended_action: Merge to one vendor record and verify which IBAN is the supplier's genuine account before the next payment run.

headline: The largest manual postings, including a EUR 78,400 capex, pass both automated layers unchecked.
mechanism: The four biggest transactions in the ledger are all keyed by hand and none is flagged by either the rule tests or the detector. The exemplar is a EUR 78,400 machinery purchase - 3.2x the next-largest item and the single biggest line in the book. The rule tests target specific bands/patterns and the detector's per-vendor deviation feature is blind to one-off vendors, so high-value manual entries fall in a coverage gap. The items look legitimate on their face but are material and un-reviewed.

evidence.what: largest line, unflagged by either layer
evidence.figure: TXN036635 EUR 78,400.00, account 1200 (Machinery), memo 'Konehankinta, kalusto', posted U-058; V-0019's only txn of the year

evidence.what: top-4 lines all human-posted and unflagged
detector blind spot
evidence.figure: V-0019 has 1 transaction, so per-vendor deviation is undefined and it cannot surface

recommended_action: Add a value-based review (e.g. every manual posting above EUR 15,000) and retrospectively confirm the 78,400 capex was approved and correctly capitalised.
